patterns.title: Interface in practice
patterns.intro: Use these live examples to build recognizable, readable interfaces. Each example uses our shared website components.
patterns.cardsRule: Give each card one purpose: a short heading, supporting information and an action when needed. Align padding across a row; allow text to wrap. Keep important information visible.
patterns.defaultCopy: Use the default card for settings summaries, explanatory content and grouped information. A plain card does not imply a click.
patterns.interactiveCopy: Use the interactive treatment for a destination or next step. Provide a real link or button, a clear label and keyboard focus. Do not nest buttons inside a whole-card link.
patterns.featureCopy: Use FeatureCard for a product capability: one icon, a short title and a concise explanation. Keep the icon decorative when the title supplies its meaning.
patterns.gradientCopy: Use a subtle gradient for an introduction or callout. Keep ordinary content on neutral surfaces and reserve strong color for meaningful emphasis.
patterns.actionsCopy: Use one primary action per decision. Outline buttons support it; text links handle navigation. A pending action keeps its label, communicates progress and prevents repeat submission.
patterns.statusCopy: Use short, descriptive labels. State connection status or hop count explicitly; color does not certify trust. Badge examples here use neutral styling.
patterns.formsCopy: Keep labels visible above fields. Explain the expected input and place a specific error next to the field. Link help and errors for screen readers. These examples are read-only.
patterns.fieldHint: Example: a short name you can recognize.
patterns.layoutCopy: Use a consistent rhythm within each component family. Stack columns on narrow screens and let translated text expand.
patterns.paddingValue: 16 px compact · 24 px standard · 32 px feature or spacious.
patterns.gridValue: 24 px between cards; 32 px between larger content groups.
patterns.radiusValue: 8 px controls · 12 px standard cards · 16 px feature cards.
patterns.widthValue: 1152 px maximum for marketing sections, with 24 px horizontal gutters.
patterns.focusCopy: Keep focus visible on every action. Test light and dark surfaces, keyboard navigation, hover and disabled states. Do not use hover alone to reveal an essential action.
patterns.disclosureCopy: Use disclosures for optional detail, with a clear question or label. Keep essential instructions outside the collapsed area. This example uses the shared AccordionList.
patterns.emptyCopy: Explain what is missing and offer a relevant next step. While loading, preserve context and announce progress. On error, keep user input and offer a specific recovery action.

standards.position: Nostr WoT brings identity, signing and Lightning payments together across compatible apps.
standards.audienceCopy: People managing their identity and payments, and developers connecting apps to signing, wallet and social-graph capabilities.
standards.characterCopy: Clear, approachable and precise. Make starting easy and keep permissions and next steps understandable.
standards.voiceCopy: Lead with the user’s action and explain its result. Name protocols where they help a developer make a decision.
standards.voiceRule: Use concrete actions instead of technical abstractions. Explain signing and payments separately; describe compatibility without promising support for every app.
standards.clearSpaceCopy: The dashed boundary shows the minimum protected area: half the symbol height on all four sides. Keep text, images and edges outside it.
standards.lightRule: Purple symbol #6366F1 + near-black lettering #111827 on a light, neutral surface.
standards.darkRule: Light-purple symbol #A5B4FC + white lettering #FFFFFF on a dark, neutral surface.
standards.logoLimits: These rules also apply to integration badges. Never recolor the logo green, yellow or red, tint the wordmark purple, stretch the geometry, add effects or rebuild the lettering. Use the symbol alone only where the brand is already identified.
standards.brandColorCopy: Purple identifies Nostr WoT. Use the lighter purple for the symbol on dark surfaces. The wordmark stays near-black or white.
standards.actionColorCopy: Primary actions use #4F46E5 with white text; hover uses #4338CA. Brand accents and action colors have different roles.
standards.statusColorCopy: Green, yellow and red describe distance or state; they never recolor our logo. Always add a label. Nostr purple belongs to the ecosystem identity, not a substitute product logo.
standards.typeRule: Use this hierarchy for the kit and comparable marketing layouts. Sizes are pixels at the default root size; the arrow shows the mobile-to-desktop change. Body text stays selectable and responsive. Keep the wordmark as its fixed SVG.
standards.imageryCopy: Use the existing tactile indigo objects, pale lavender surfaces and fine orbit lines. Keep mint and coral accents restrained. Use genuine screenshots to demonstrate product UI; illustrations explain concepts.
standards.homeAlt: Indigo objects on a pale lavender background.
standards.homeCaption: Brand atmosphere: spacious, tactile and free of embedded text.
standards.developersAlt: Developer-themed objects in the existing illustration style.
standards.developersCaption: Developer content: use the matching asset rather than inventing a second visual style.
standards.iconsCopy: Reuse the shared icon family at 20–24 px in controls. Feature illustrations may be larger. Align icons optically with text; decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology and icon-only actions need a label.
standards.compositionCopy: Build one clear focal point with aligned text and generous space. Keep copy and original vectors separate from imagery so they can be localized. Use subtle transitions and honor reduced motion. Essential content must remain visible without animation.
